evals.prompt: With jvm-patterns loaded, implement a small behaviour change in a Java or Kotlin module in a target repo (e.g. add a method that validates input and can fail).
evals.expected_output: A scoped change that avoids null (Optional / Kotlin null-safety, no !!), closes resources with try-with-resources/use, adds JUnit tests covering the behaviour plus a boundary and an exception case, compiles cleanly (correct imports/types), and follows the configured formatter/linter conventions.
assertions: Null is handled via Optional or Kotlin null-safety (no Kotlin !! and no obvious NPE risk)
Resources are closed with try-with-resources (Java) or use (Kotlin)
JUnit tests cover the happy path plus a boundary and an exception case
No exception is swallowed (no empty catch), and the change has no obvious compile error (correct imports, types, and signatures)
No existing test is weakened, skipped, or deleted

evals.prompt: With jvm-patterns loaded, add code that shares state across threads, keyed by a small value type (e.g. a record or data class used as a map key).
evals.expected_output: Thread-safe shared state (immutability or proper synchronization/concurrent types), a value-type key (record/data class) with consistent equals/hashCode, resources closed, and deterministic tests covering an error path.
assertions: Shared state is thread-safe (immutable or properly synchronized/concurrent types)
Resources are released (try-with-resources / use); no leak
Tests are deterministic (no real network/clock) and cover an error/exception path
equals/hashCode stay consistent if value types are added or changed

component.purpose: The JVM (Java/Kotlin) conventions and toolchain the software-engineer/qa-engineer (and the code-review lint aspect) apply when the detected stack is JVM; a lean, loaded-on-demand knowledge pack exercised through the software-engineer's Tier-2.
